chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā Ja'far عليه السلام saying: The 'iddah and menstruation are entrusted to the women.

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women, whose report is relied upon in these matters
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: menstruation, a legally consequential state related to purity and family law
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: the waiting period whose determination affects family law rulings
key_terms.سَمِعْتُ: I heard, indicating direct transmission from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.يَقُولُ: he says, introducing the Imam’s legal statement

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, whose word is accepted regarding menstruation and 'iddah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that matters of 'iddah and menstruation are referred to women, meaning their word is relied upon regarding these conditions. It is significant in fiqh because it establishes women’s authority in reporting these personal states relevant to legal rulings.
